description: Electronic engineering student from Lima building a tool for farmers in Moquegua, Peru, using NASA POWER data (frost, soil moisture, rainfall) for the farms challenge. I'm looking for a teammate FROM Moquegua who knows local crops and farmers, plus anyone with data analysis, web or design skills. Spanish-speaking team, working remotely. Message me and we start tonight: submission opens tomorrow at 9:00.
summary: ChacraTest is a decision-support tool for crop rotation in the highlands of Moquegua, Peru, where farmers depend on a short rainy season and face droughts and frosts. Instead of recommending a rotation from averages, it stress-tests each rotation against every growing season from 1991 to 2025 using NASA POWER rainfall, root-zone soil moisture and minimum temperature. It shows in how many seasons a rotation would have failed from lack of water or frost, tests whether El Niño years differ significantly from the rest (stating the small sample size), and adapts the result to the farmer’s priorities in plain language.
details:
PROBLEM

In the highlands of Moquegua, Peru, rain is concentrated in a few months: at Carumas, 86% of the October–April rainfall in the NASA POWER record falls from December to March. Rainfall also varies a lot between seasons, from 35 mm in 1991 to 178 mm in 2005 (NASA POWER grid values). A crop rotation that looks reasonable on average can still fail in the bad seasons.

WHAT IT DOES

ChacraTest is a decision-support tool for comparing crop rotations. For Carumas, it replays each candidate rotation through every 3-season window in 35 real October–April seasons (1991–2025, 33 windows) and counts how often at least one season would have been flagged for lack of rain or for frost. With our default settings, between 55% and 70% of windows had a flagged season, depending on the rotation, and no rotation wins on every criterion: the ranking changes with the weight given to soil health. The page also shows a monthly rain and frost-night table, a sowing-month planner, and a plain-language explanation of the result that can be read aloud (generated by fixed rules, not by an AI model). It works in English and Spanish. ChacraTest compares options; it does not forecast.

HOW IT WORKS

1. A Python script (Google Colab) downloads daily rainfall (PRECTOTCORR) and minimum temperature (T2M_MIN) from the NASA POWER API (community AG) for Carumas (-16.8096, -70.6950). Root-zone wetness (GWETROOT) was also downloaded but is not used in the score.

2. Data are grouped by growing season (October–April) and by month.

3. Because NASA POWER rainfall is a coarse-grid estimate, "dry" and "very dry" seasons are defined with percentiles of the series, not absolute millimetres; frost nights are counted at 0, -2 and -4 °C. All thresholds can be edited on the page.

4. Each crop (potato, faba bean, quinoa, barley) has editable water and frost assumptions. Three example rotations are compared: potato-faba bean-barley, potato-quinoa-barley, and barley repeated three times as a reference.

5. A simple soil rule adds a point for a legume and subtracts one for repeating a crop.

6. A static web page (HTML/JavaScript, no server) shows the results, with approximate 95% ranges; there are only 35 seasons. Live page: https://chacratest.vercel.app/

7. The page includes a Mann-Whitney comparison of El Niño and other seasons that runs when a list of El Niño seasons is entered. We did not complete that analysis for this submission.

LIMITATIONS AND VALIDATION

- NASA POWER cells are about 50 km wide and may miss a local frost. Its rainfall at Carumas (about 130 mm per year on average, about 116 mm median; one very high monthly value in September 2022 raises the mean) looks lower than the ~300 mm per year quoted in workshop material; we have not checked this against a weather station.

- Thresholds are reference values and are NOT validated locally. Potato frost limits are informed by an INIA test on native potato accessions and quinoa limits by an INIAP frost study; faba bean and barley limits are assumptions without a source yet.

- This is a historical stress-test, not a forecast or a sowing calendar. Crop calendars must come from INIA or Midagri.

- Planned validation: a low-cost field temperature node (ESP32) compared with NASA POWER, and a review by a local agronomist. These are designed on paper, not built.

IMPACT

Intended users (a hypothesis we have not tested yet): extension technicians and user boards who advise farmers in the highlands of Moquegua. ChacraTest can help them compare rotations against 35 real seasons before sowing and discuss the trade-off between climate risk and soil health. Future steps: (1) validate the thresholds locally, with a field temperature node (ESP32) and a local agronomist; (2) add more districts and crop calendars from INIA/Midagri; (3) add a chat assistant inside the page, for example built with n8n, that only explains the results ChacraTest computes, without adding its own numbers or sowing advice; (4) consider delivery through Telegram or WhatsApp, after checking their current costs and rules; (5) consider machine learning or profit scenarios only if we obtain enough data (yields, costs, prices, more sites) to improve on the current simple method. These are ideas for future versions; none is designed or built yet.

TOOLS

Python (requests, pandas), Google Colab, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, GitHub and GitHub Pages, PowerPoint.

AI ASSISTANCE

We used an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) to discuss approaches, research background material, review code and text, and draft specific parts: the monthly data script, the sowing-month planner, and the slides. The core analysis code was written by the team. The team ran the code, checked the numbers against the data, and made these decisions: we worked with Moquegua, the region of our event, and used Carumas as a highland test point; we chose potato, faba bean, quinoa and barley as example crops and three example rotations; we kept relative thresholds (dry at the 25th percentile, very dry at the 10th, frost-bad at the 75th) because NASA POWER rainfall at Carumas looks lower than the station figures quoted in workshop material; we made the monthly view central; and we left out profit and yield forecasts, sowing recommendations and any claim of local validation.
The English narration of the demo video was generated with a text-to-speech AI voice (ElevenLabs), from a script drafted with the AI assistant and reviewed by the team.
dataRefs: NASA POWER, daily point API (community AG): PRECTOTCORR, T2M_MIN, GWETROOT
